There are also people who like spring better than autumn.

definitions.text: The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
One of the genae, flat areas on the sides of a trilobite's cephalon.

examples.text: He had the cheek to ask me to help him.
I wouldn't have the cheek to say such a thing.
I use the word in a tongue-in-cheek fashion.

definitions.text: The act or process of (physically or figuratively) attaching.
A strong bonding with or fondness for someone or something.

examples.text: Some cats only form a strong attachment to one human.
According to Buddhism, the primary cause of suffering is attachment.
She had a great attachment to that old house.

definitions.text: A thing that holds.
A person who temporarily or permanently possesses something.

examples.text: You need to use a pot holder when handling hot pots.
Is Algeria a massive holder of gold reserves?
I'm a holder of ABC Travel Insurance.

definitions.text: Of or pertaining to the sun; proceeding from the sun
Born under the predominant influence of the sun.

examples.text: The nearest star to our solar system is Proxima Centauri.
The problem is that solar energy just costs too much.
The Sun is in the center of the solar system.

definitions.text: To smile, parting the lips so as to show the teeth.
To express by grinning.
A smile in which the lips are parted to reveal the teeth.

examples.text: The more I spoke, the wider her grin became.
He said it with a grin on his face.
He had a big grin on his face.

definitions.text: A shrub of the genus Rosa, with red, pink, white or yellow flowers.
A flower of the rose plant.
Having a purplish-red or pink colour. See rosy.
To make rose-coloured; to redden or flush.

examples.text: The girl brought me a red and a white rose.
I half rose to my feet to leave my seat.
She rose to her feet with tears in her eyes.

definitions.text: (grammar, narrow sense) A word that can be used to refer to a person, animal, place, thing, phenomenon, substance, quality, or idea
To convert a word to a noun.

examples.text: This word is both a noun and a verb.
I know the sentence must start with a noun.
This word should be treated as a noun in this case.

definitions.text: Happening by good luck or favorable chance.
Auspicious.

examples.text: He was fortunate to find the book he had lost.
He was so fortunate as to find a good job.
I was pretty fortunate to be able to do that.

definitions.text: Good; in acceptable, if not excellent condition.
In good health, unharmed.
Used to indicate acknowledgement or acceptance; OK.

examples.text: Alright, I know what I was supposed to do now.
It is alright, you don't need to see me off.
If you think it's alright with you, say I'm fine.

definitions.text: Unwilling to do work or make an effort; disinclined to exertion.
Causing or characterised by idleness; relaxed or leisurely.
To laze, act in a lazy manner.
A lazy person.

examples.text: He is not as lazy a student as you think.
For one thing he is lazy, for another he drinks.
He was dismissed on the grounds that he was lazy.

definitions.text: "Hello!" or an equivalent greeting.
A greeting (salutation) said when meeting someone or acknowledging someone’s arrival or presence.

examples.text: Hello. This is Joe Carlton. May I speak to Michael?
When you see the Popescus, please say hello from us.
Hello. Is it possible to speak with Mrs Johnson please?

definitions.text: A need or compelling desire for food.
(by extension) Any strong desire.
To be in need of food.

examples.text: I ate a large dinner and my hunger was satisfied.
While feeding only on hope, you can die of hunger.
The prisoners are threatening to go on a hunger strike.

definitions.text: To make a pledge to (someone); to promise, guarantee (someone of something); to assure.
To make sure or certain of something (usually some future event or condition).

examples.text: I would like to insure this package.
I'd like to insure this, please.
What can we insure ourselves against?

definitions.text: To feel shame; to be ashamed.
To make ashamed; to shame.
Feeling shame or guilt.

examples.text: I am ashamed of not having been kind to her.
A man of sense would be ashamed to do so.
I think being poor is nothing to be ashamed of.

definitions.text: To encounter or discover by accident; to happen upon.
To encounter or discover something being searched for; to locate.

examples.text: I found it best to say nothing about the matter.
I tried to answer the question, which I found impossible.
I tried to solve the problem, which I found impossible.

definitions.text: An individual post to a blog.
(originally nonce word) A cocktail or punch served at science fiction conventions. Ingredients vary for different conventions.
To contribute to a blog.

examples.text: You didn't tell them what we wrote in that blog.
You didn't tell them what they wrote in that blog.
In my spare time, I write articles for my blog.

definitions.text: The condition producing the sensation of thirst.
A want and eager desire (for something); a craving or longing.
To be thirsty.

examples.text: The man was dying—dying from hunger and from thirst.
The man died of thirst in a dry country.
Thirst is the feeling of needing to drink something.
